title: How do you spend your free time?
titleTranslate: 你如何度过空闲时间？
text:
Peter: Hey, Yaming!
What are you up to?
Yaming: Hi, Peter.
I'm doing calligraphy.
Peter: It's beautiful!
What are you writing?
Yaming: It's a poem by Li Bai.
My grandmother taught me how to write it.
Peter: What's this character?
Yaming: It's yue.
It means "moon".
Peter: It's nice!
I like watching you write like that.
But it looks difficult.
Yaming: Well, the first step is always the hardest.
When I started to do calligraphy, I spent hours practising single strokes.
Peter: I know how that feels!
My dad's teaching me to play the guitar.
It's difficult, but he always encourages me not to give up.
Yaming: Exactly.
Now I do calligraphy to relax.
I even like how the ink smells!
Why did you choose to play the guitar?
Peter: I think playing the guitar is cool.
Will you teach me to write a poem?
I can teach you to play a song in return.
Yaming: It's a deal!

How did you get into painting?
I saw my mother paint.
I decided to give it a go.
textTranslate:
彼得：嘿，亚明！
你在做什么呢？
亚明：你好，彼得。
我正在练习书法。
彼得：真漂亮！
你在写什么？
亚明：这是一首李白的诗。
是我奶奶教我写的。

彼得：我懂那种感觉！
我爸爸正在教我弹吉他。
虽然很难，但他总是鼓励我不要放弃。

我甚至喜欢墨水的味道！
你为什么选择弹吉他？
彼得：我觉得弹吉他很酷。
你能教我写一首诗吗？
我可以教你弹一首曲子作为交换。
亚明：一言为定！

你是怎么开始学习绘画的？
我看到我妈妈画画。
于是我决定试一试。

title: How can a hobby improve your life?
titleTranslate: 爱好如何改善你的生活？
text:
Facts are statements that are true.
On the other hand, opinions express a feeling or belief.
They may or may not be true.
Look for key words like "think" or "believe" to help you identify whether a statement is an opinion.

When work or school is over, what do you do to pass the time?
Do you spend time on your hobbies?
Reading or listening to music can help us to calm down after a busy day.
Physical hobbies, such as playing tennis or doing yoga, can help us to keep fit.
And some hobbies are creative.
For example, people sometimes paint pictures to remember a beautiful landscape or object, or reduce stress.

Luca Bruno likes to be creative in his free time.
But he doesn't make art or write stories.
Instead, this Italian teenager finds it fun to make mobile phone apps.
He thinks that apps can be a great way to help people.
He started programming when he was ten, after he read about famous businessmen who started out as programmers.
His latest app allows people around the world to find study partners for learning Italian.
They can learn Italian and make friends at the same time!

"It gives me such a sense of achievement to see people using the app," says Luca.
"I believe I'm helping people around the world to learn Italian!"

Some people prefer not to make things.
They prefer to collect them!
In India, Maya Badal doesn't collect coins or stamps.
Instead, this teenage girl collects postcards!

"I know some people think postcards are rather old-fashioned, but I think they're a good way to learn about different places," Maya says.
"I think it's interesting to see the beautiful buildings and landscapes in foreign countries."

Maya's first postcard shows the Mogao Caves in Dunhuang.
Her dad sent it to her when she was five, and she liked it so much that she put it up on her bedroom wall!
Now there are over one hundred postcards from thirty-two countries on Maya's walls.
She dreams of travelling to these places in the future!

I have many free-time activities, like painting, writing poems, and reading.
But my favourite free-time activity is horse riding.

When I was six, I visited my grandfather's farm, and he took me to ride a horse.
It was such an amazing experience!
Now I ride my favourite horse, Nini, at his farm every weekend.

I love horse riding because I enjoy being in nature.
Horse riding also helps me stay fit.
But most importantly, it lets me spend time with Nini!
She's my best friend.
She's happy to see me whenever I visit, especially when I bring her some carrots for a snack!
I'm lucky to have her in my life.
textTranslate:
事实是指符合客观实际的陈述。
另一方面，观点表达的是感受或看法。
观点可能是正确的，也可能是错误的。
留意“认为”“相信”等关键词，帮助你判断一句话是否表达观点。

工作或放学后，你通常做些什么来消磨时间？
你会把时间花在自己的兴趣爱好上吗？
读书或听音乐能帮助我们在一天的忙碌之后平静下来。
体育类的兴趣爱好，如打网球或做瑜伽，能帮助我们保持健康。
有些兴趣爱好还需要发挥创造力。
例如，人们有时会画下美丽的风景或物品，以留住美好回忆或缓解压力。

卢卡·布鲁诺喜欢在空闲时间发挥创造力。
但他不创作艺术品，也不写故事。
相反，这位意大利少年觉得制作手机应用程序很有趣。
他认为，应用程序是帮助人们的一种好方式。
十岁时，他读到了几位从程序员起步的著名企业家的故事，于是开始学习编程。
他最新推出的应用程序能帮助世界各地的人找到学习意大利语的伙伴。
他们可以同时学习意大利语、交朋友！

“看到人们使用这款应用程序，我真有成就感。”卢卡说。
“我相信自己正在帮助世界各地的人学习意大利语！”

有些人不喜欢制作东西。
他们更喜欢收藏东西！
在印度，玛雅·巴达尔既不收藏硬币，也不收集邮票。
相反，这位少女收集的是明信片！

“我知道有些人认为明信片有些过时，但我觉得它们是了解不同地方的好方式。”玛雅说。
“我觉得欣赏外国优美的建筑和风景很有意思。”

玛雅收藏的第一张明信片上印着敦煌莫高窟。
她五岁时，爸爸把这张明信片寄给了她。她非常喜欢，于是把它贴在卧室的墙上！
如今，玛雅的墙上贴着一百多张来自三十二个国家的明信片。
她梦想着将来亲自去这些地方旅行！

我有许多空闲活动，比如绘画、写诗和阅读。
但我最喜欢的空闲活动是骑马。

六岁时，我去了爷爷的农场，他带我骑了马。
那是一次令人惊叹的经历！
现在，每个周末我都会到他的农场骑我最喜欢的马“妮妮”。

我喜欢骑马，因为我喜欢身处大自然之中。
骑马还能帮助我保持健康。
但最重要的是，它让我能和妮妮共度时光！
她是我最好的朋友。
每当我去看她时，她都很开心，尤其是我还会带些胡萝卜给她当零食！
有她陪伴我的生活，我很幸运。

title: The Art and History of Chinese Characters
titleTranslate: 汉字的艺术与历史
text:
Chinese characters are one of the oldest writing systems in the world.
Some Chinese characters come from pictographs.
A pictograph is a pictorial symbol for a word or phrase.
For example, in the Chinese character "旦 (dan)", the upper part refers to the sun, while the lower part stands for the sea level (or the horizon).
The character, meaning "daybreak" or "beginning", uses the two parts to make a picture of the sun rising above the sea.
Another common category of Chinese characters is the system of compound characters.
Two or more characters are combined in one character to create a compound character with a new meaning.
Some of these are easy to understand.
For example, a tree is 木, a group of trees is 林, and a forest is 森.

The art of Chinese calligraphy came into being with the writing of Chinese characters.
Chinese calligraphy is usually done with an ink brush that is usually made of goat hair.
Chinese calligraphy is a unique Chinese visual art of lines and dots.
Over thousands of years, the style of Chinese calligraphy has continually evolved.
In general, there are five major styles: seal script (Zhuanshu), clerical script (Lishu), regular script (Kaishu), cursive script (Caoshu), and semi-cursive script (Xingshu).
There are many famous calligraphers throughout Chinese history, like Wang Xizhi (303-361), Yan Zhenqing (709-785), Su Shi (1037- 1101), and Zhang Xu (8th century).
textTranslate:
汉字是世界上最古老的书写系统之一。
有些汉字源于象形文字。
象形文字是表示某个词或短语的图像符号。
例如，在汉字“旦（dan）”中，上半部分表示太阳，下半部分表示海平面（或地平线）。
这个字意为“黎明”或“开始”，利用这两个部分构成了一幅太阳从海面升起的图画。
汉字的另一个常见类别是合体字。
将两个或两个以上的字组合成一个字，就形成了具有新意义的合体字。
有些合体字很容易理解。
例如，树是“木”，成片的树是“林”，森林是“森”。

中国书法艺术随着汉字的使用而产生。
中国书法通常使用毛笔书写，毛笔一般用山羊毛制成。
中国书法是一门由线和点构成的中国独特视觉艺术。
数千年来，中国书法的风格不断发展演变。
一般来说，主要有五大书体：篆书（Zhuanshu）、隶书（Lishu）、楷书（Kaishu）、草书（Caoshu）和行书（Xingshu）。
中国历史上有许多著名书法家，如王羲之（303-361）、颜真卿（709-785）、苏轼（1037-1101）和张旭（8世纪）。

title: What should we do when we don't feel well?
titleTranslate: 身体不适时，我们应该怎么办？
text:
Doctor: Take a seat, Helen.
How are you feeling?
Helen: Not good ...
I have a runny nose and a fever.
Doctor: Let me take your temperature ...
Oh, it's quite high.
Helen: Yes, it started yesterday.
I felt so cold, and I didn't have much energy.
When I tried to get out of bed, I almost fell and hurt myself.
My throat hurts too.
Doctor: Let's see.
Yes, the back of your throat looks very red.
We'll need to do a test, but I believe you have the flu.
It's flu season.
Helen: What should I do, Doctor?
Doctor: You should take some medicine and drink enough water.
Helen: OK, thank you.
Can I go to school tomorrow?
Doctor: No, you should rest at home.
When you're outside, please wear a mask.
It stops us from passing the flu virus to others easily.
Helen: I will!
Doctor: And remember, your health is in your hands.
If you take good care of yourself, you'll get better soon.

You should / shouldn't exercise.
What should I do?
Don't go to school today.
Can I go to school tomorrow?
textTranslate:
医生：坐下吧，海伦。
你感觉怎么样？
海伦：不太好……
我流鼻涕，还发烧。
医生：让我给你量一下体温……
哦，体温相当高。
海伦：是的，昨天开始发烧的。
我觉得非常冷，而且没什么力气。
我试图起床时，差点摔倒并弄伤自己。
我的喉咙也疼。
医生：让我看看。
是的，你的喉咙后部看起来很红。
我们需要做一项检查，但我认为你得了流感。
现在是流感高发期。
海伦：医生，我该怎么办？
医生：你应该吃些药，并喝足够的水。
海伦：好的，谢谢您。
我明天能去上学吗？
医生：不行，你应该待在家休息。
在室外时，请戴上口罩。
口罩可以防止我们轻易将流感病毒传染给别人。
海伦：我会的！
医生：还要记住，你的健康掌握在自己手中。

title: How should we stay safe?
titleTranslate: 我们应该如何保证安全？
text:
James lived in the city with his friend Allen.
It was their first time living away from their families, and they enjoyed learning how to do many things themselves.
One Saturday, James decided to make fried chicken.
First, he poured oil into a pan.
Then he turned on the stove and left the oil to heat while he prepared the chicken.
Just then, he heard the front door open, followed by the sound of Allen singing.
"Guess what," Allen called out happily.
"We won!"
"No way!"
James followed him into the living room.
He wanted to hear all about the football game!
Suddenly, Allen stopped talking and looked up.
"Hey, do you smell something burning?"
"Oh no!"
They both rushed back into the kitchen.
The pan was on fire!
Large flames were jumping into the air.
In a panic, James turned off the stove at once.
But he was so close to the pan that a flame jumped onto his shirt.
James cried out and threw himself to the floor.
He put out the fire by rolling on the ground, but the pan was still burning!
"Get water, quick!" he shouted.
Allen was about to do so when he stopped short.
Thanks to the first aid and safety classes he took at school, he knew that water could make oil fires much worse!
Instead, he rushed to get the fire extinguisher.
In seconds, the fire in the burning pan was put out.

"Are you OK?"
Allen asked his friend.
"I think so," James said.
It was lucky that his shirt wasn't too thin!
His arm was red, but it didn't hurt very much.
"Maybe we should eat out tonight," James said as he ran cool water over his arm.
"Sure, we could do that.
What do you want?"
"Anything but fried chicken," he said sadly.

One Saturday, Julie invited Mark and Lucy to her house for lunch.
Her parents weren't home, so they had it all to themselves.
They ordered pizza, salad, and juice.
But in the middle of the meal, Mark started to feel strange.
His face felt warm, and his throat felt tight.
"Were there any peanuts in our food?" he asked nervously.
"I think I tasted peanuts in the salad," said Julie.
"What's the matter?"
"Oh no, I'm allergic to peanuts!"
Mark cried.
His friends jumped into action and took him to the hospital at once.
At the hospital, Mark's friends told Dr Cooper what happened, and she gave Mark some medicine right away.
When Mark felt better, the doctor asked him some questions and gave him some advice.
"I'll take better care of myself from now on," Mark promised.
It was a day he would never forget.

I feel much better now.

詹姆斯和他的朋友艾伦住在城里。
这是他们第一次离开家人独立生活，他们很享受学习亲手做很多事情。
一天星期六，詹姆斯决定做炸鸡。
首先，他把油倒进锅里。
然后，他打开炉灶，让油加热，同时准备鸡肉。
就在这时，他听见前门打开，随后传来艾伦的歌声。
“猜猜看是什么事，”艾伦开心地喊道。
“我们赢了！”
“不可能！”
詹姆斯跟着他走进客厅。
他想听艾伦讲讲足球比赛的精彩过程！
突然，艾伦停止说话，抬起头来。

“当然，我们可以这么做。
你想吃什么？”
“除了炸鸡，什么都行。”他难过地说。

一个星期六，朱莉邀请马克和露西到家里吃午饭。
她的父母不在家，所以他们可以自由自在地待着。
他们点了披萨、沙拉和果汁。

朋友们立即行动起来，赶紧把他送到医院。

title: Exercising for Health
titleTranslate: 为健康而锻炼
text:
No matter how busy their life is, a lot of people still make time to exercise to improve their health.
People can choose to do many different kinds of exercise.
Some prefer outdoor activities like cycling, jogging, climbing, square dancing, playing tennis, and playing badminton.
Others love to work out in a gym, such as yoga and swimming, to relax after a busy and tiring day.
After doing exercise, people feel happy, relaxed, and full of energy.

Two popular outdoor activities are taijiquan and square dancing.
As a traditional sport in China, taijiquan is loved by both the old and young.
In the early mornings, while jogging in a beautiful park, you may find people doing taijiquan along to music.
Square dancing is also popular in China.
In the evenings, while walking in the town square, you might see people doing square dancing.
You might want to dance together with them too!
textTranslate:
无论生活多么忙碌，许多人仍会抽出时间锻炼，以改善健康状况。
人们可以选择许多不同类型的锻炼方式。
有些人喜欢骑自行车、慢跑、登山、跳广场舞、打网球和打羽毛球等户外活动。
另一些人喜欢在健身房锻炼，如练瑜伽和游泳，以放松自己，舒缓一天忙碌而疲惫的身体。
锻炼后，人们会感到快乐、放松并充满活力。

太极拳和广场舞是两项颇受欢迎的户外活动。
作为中国的传统体育项目，太极拳深受老年人和年轻人的喜爱。
清晨，在美丽的公园里慢跑时，你可能会看见人们伴随着音乐打太极拳。
广场舞在中国也很受欢迎。
傍晚，在城市广场散步时，你可能会看到人们跳广场舞。
你也许还想和他们一起跳呢！

title: What makes you upset?
titleTranslate: 什么会使你感到难过？
text:
Lily: What's wrong, Judy?
Judy: Well, my parents aren't happy with my grades.
Lily: Really?
Weren't they pretty good this term?
Judy: Yeah, but my parents have very high standards.
They often compare me with my cousin, Kate.
She gets better grades, plays the piano well, often wins awards ...
I'm sorry to hear that.
But look on the bright side.
I'm sure your parents just want you to do well, although they may not show it.
Judy: I know my parents love me, but sometimes I think they love Kate more.
Why don't you talk to them?
Until you talk to them, they might not know how you feel.
Judy: I'm afraid I'll cry if we talk.
How about writing them a letter so that you can get your message across clearly?
Judy: Oh, that's a good idea.
Lily: Writing things down can also make you feel better.
Judy: Thanks!
Just talking to you makes me feel better already!

There are many things you can do when you feel stressed.
First, you can take a break from what you are doing.
This will help you clear your mind.
You can listen to music or go for a walk.
Next, share your problems with someone you trust instead of shutting yourself away.
The person might not have any advice for you, but talking about your problems can help you feel better.
Lastly, remember to take care of yourself.
Eat healthy food, exercise, and get enough sleep.
These three things alone are great for reducing stress!
textTranslate:
朱莉：怎么了，朱迪？
朱迪：嗯，我父母对我的成绩不满意。
朱莉：真的吗？
这学期的成绩不是挺好的吗？
朱迪：是的，但我父母的要求很高。

朱迪：我怕我们一谈我就会哭。
不如给他们写封信，这样你就能把自己的意思清楚地表达出来。
朱迪：哦，这是个好主意。
莉莉：把事情写下来也能让你感觉好一些。
朱迪：谢谢你！
只是和你聊了聊，我就已经感觉好多了！

感到压力时，你可以做很多事情。
首先，你可以暂时放下正在做的事情，休息一下。
这有助于你理清思路。
你可以听音乐，也可以出去散步。
接下来，把你的问题告诉一个你信任的人，不要把自己封闭起来。
这个人可能没法给你什么建议，但谈谈你的问题能让你感觉好一些。
最后，别忘了照顾好自己。
吃健康的食物，坚持锻炼，并保证充足的睡眠。
仅这三件事就足以 greatly 缓解压力了！

title: How can we stay positive?
titleTranslate: 我们如何保持积极乐观？
text:
When the bell rang, Matt entered the classroom with a heavy heart.
"Hey, Matt," his best friend Tom greeted him.
He and Tom were in the school's basketball team.
"Why the long face?
Are you still feeling blue about Saturday night's game?"
Tom asked.
"Of course I am," Matt said quietly.
He didn't dare to look at Tom as he spoke.
"I'm really sorry about letting everybody down.
The other team got those points because of me."
"Don't be too hard on yourself!"
Tom said.
"Although you pushed their player, it was just an accident.
Everyone knows that!"
Tom was a good friend.
But Matt knew the referee didn't share Tom's opinion.
When the referee saw Matt push another player, he gave the other team two free throws.
Matt was as shocked as anyone else when the accident happened, but it was too late.
He couldn't take it back.
"I guess we have to respect his decision," Matt said after a while.
"But we had a good chance to win until I made that mistake.
Why wasn't I more careful?"
"Listen, Matt," said Tom, "try to look on the bright side.
The other team is the best in our area, but our scores were really close.
I'm proud of us, and I know our coach and everyone else in our school are as well."
Matt felt a bit better.
"Thanks, Tom.
I guess it's just hard to lose."
"Hey, you can't win them all," said Tom.
"It's more important to learn from your mistakes so that you don't repeat them in future.
We'll keep working together as a team.
One for all, and all for one, right?"
"You're right.
If we pull together, we should win next time," Matt smiled.
He was lucky to have a friend like Tom!

I find it hard to make friends.
I'm afraid to talk to others, although I want to get to know them better.
textTranslate:
铃声响起时，马特心情沉重地走进教室。
“嘿，马特。”他的好朋友汤姆跟他打招呼。
他和汤姆都是学校篮球队的队员。
“为什么愁眉苦脸的？
星期六晚上的比赛让你到现在还很难过吗？”
汤姆问道。
“当然难过了。”马特轻声说。
说话时，他不敢看汤姆。
“真的很抱歉，我让所有人都失望了。
对方队得到那些分数都是因为我。”
“别太苛责自己！”
汤姆说。
“虽然你推了对方的球员，但那只是意外。
大家都是这么认为的！”
汤姆是个好朋友。
但马特知道，裁判并不赞同汤姆的看法。
裁判看到马特推了另一名球员后，判给对方两次罚球机会。
意外发生时，马特和其他人一样震惊，但已经太晚了。
他无法收回自己做过的事。
“我想，我们只能尊重裁判的决定。”过了一会儿，马特说。
“不过，在我犯错之前，我们本来很有机会获胜。
我为什么不能再小心一点呢？”
“听着，马特，”汤姆说，“试着往好处想想。
对方队是我们这个地区最强的队，但我们的比分确实很接近。
我为我们感到骄傲，我相信我们的教练和学校里其他所有人也都是如此。”
马特感觉好了一些。
“谢谢你，汤姆。
我想，输掉比赛确实不好受。”
“嘿，你不可能赢下所有比赛。”汤姆说。
“更重要的是从错误中吸取教训，这样以后就不会再犯同样的错误。
我们还要作为一个团队继续努力。
团结一心，互帮互助，对吧？”
“你说得对。
只要我们齐心协力，下次就应该能赢。”马特笑着说。
他能有汤姆这样的朋友，真幸运！

我觉得交朋友很难。
我害怕和别人交谈，尽管我想更多地了解他们。

title: Helping Crops Thrive: A Lesson from Mencius
titleTranslate: 帮助庄稼茁壮成长：孟子的教诲
text:
Mencius, a wise Chinese man from ancient times, once shared a story with a valuable lesson.

Once upon a time, there lived a farmer who grew some crops.
He often felt that his neighbour's crops grew faster than his.
Every day, he would visit his field, hoping that his crops would grow taller than his neighbour's.

Many days passed, but the farmer's crops did not grow any faster.
He walked around the field unhappily and thought, "I must find a way to help them grow faster."
One day he had an idea.
He began pulling up the plants to make them look as tall as his neighbour's.
When evening arrived, he returned home, tired but happy.
He told his son, "Today, I worked hard, and helped our crops grow a little faster!"

His son was puzzled by his father's words.
When he rushed to the field the next day, he found nothing but dead crops.
textTranslate:
孟子是中国古代一位睿智的人，他曾讲过一个蕴含宝贵道理的故事。

从前，有一位农民种了一些庄稼。
他常常觉得，邻居家的庄稼长得比自家的快。
他每天都会到田里查看，希望自家的庄稼长得比邻居家的更高。

许多天过去了，但农民的庄稼并没有长得更快。
他闷闷不乐地绕着田地走，心想：“我必须想个办法，让它们长得更快。”
有一天，他想到了一个办法。
他开始把植株往上拔，让它们看起来和邻居家的庄稼一样高。
傍晚时分，他筋疲力尽地回到家，却很开心。
他对儿子说：“今天我卖力干活了，还帮助咱们的庄稼长高了一点呢！”

儿子对父亲的话感到困惑不解。
第二天，他急忙赶到田里，发现只剩下枯死的庄稼。

title: What is amazing about nature?
titleTranslate: 大自然有哪些神奇之处？
text:
Yaming: Welcome back, Ella!
How was your trip?
It was great!
We saw the Hukou Waterfall on the Yellow River.
Is that the longest river in China?
Yaming: No, the Yangtze River is the longest river in China.
It travels the farthest and is about 6,300 kilometres long.
The Yellow River is 5,464 kilometres long and is the second longest.
By the way, do you know why it's called the Yellow River?
Because it's yellow?
Yaming: Right.
Some parts of the river carry brown and yellow earth.
That's interesting!
I like learning about rivers.
My favourite is the Nile.
Did you know it's the longest river in the world?
Yaming: Yes, it's 6,671 kilometres long.
It's very important in Egypt's history.
That's right.
Both the Nile and the Yellow River helped ancient civilizations to develop.
And they're still very important today.
Yaming: Yes.
In China, we even call the Yellow River our "mother river"!
We should protect them at all costs.

Could you tell me more about China, Yaming?
Yaming: Sure!
What would you like to know?
What's the biggest desert in China?
Yaming: It's the Taklimakan Desert.
Do you know ...?

What is the biggest desert in the world?
It is the Sahara Desert.
It is about 9,000,000 square How big is it? kilometres in size.
Where is the deepest point in the ocean?
It is in the Mariana Trench.
How deep is it?
It is about 11,000 metres deep.
Some deep-sea animals are blind, but they can "see" as well as others.
Mount Qomolangma is one of the greatest wonders of the world, and it is still growing taller.
The Yangtze River travels the farthest in China and is about 6,300 kilometres long.
textTranslate:
亚明：欢迎回来，艾拉！
旅途怎么样？
非常棒！
我们参观了黄河上的壶口瀑布。
那是中国最长的河流吗？
亚明：不，长江是中国最长的河流。
它的流程最长，全长约6,300千米。
黄河全长5,464千米，是第二长的河流。
顺便问一下，你知道它为什么叫作黄河吗？
因为它是黄色的吗？
亚明：没错。
黄河有些河段夹带着棕色和黄色的泥土。
真有意思！
我喜欢了解有关河流的知识。
我最喜欢的是尼罗河。
你知道吗，它是世界上最长的河流？
亚明：是的，全长6,671千米。
它在埃及历史上非常重要。
正是如此。
尼罗河和黄河都促进了古代文明的发展。
而且直到今天，它们仍然非常重要。
亚明：是的。
在中国，我们甚至把黄河称为我们的“母亲河”！
我们应该不惜一切代价保护它们。

亚明，你能给我多讲讲中国吗？
亚明：当然可以！
你想知道些什么？
中国最大的沙漠是什么？
亚明：是塔克拉玛干沙漠。
你知道……吗？

世界上最大的沙漠是什么？
是撒哈拉沙漠。
它的面积约为9,000,000平方公里。有多大？
海洋最深处在哪里？
在马里亚纳海沟。
它有多深？
它深约11,000米。
有些深海动物是瞎的，但它们也能像其他动物一样“看”东西。
珠穆朗玛峰是世界最大的奇迹之一，而且至今仍在不断增高。
长江是中国流程最长的河流，全长约6,300千米。

title: Why do we explore nature?
titleTranslate: 我们为什么要探索大自然？
text:
To most people, Mount Qomolangma is one of the greatest wonders of the world.
On the highest place on earth, you will feel like you are able to touch the sky.
But only the best climbers reach the top, and that is only if they survive the terrible conditions first.
On the mountain, temperatures can fall to –30 degrees.
Climbers must also deal with thin air, high cliffs, and changeable weather.

Before 1960, no one was able to reach the top of Qomolangma from the northern side.
Mountain climbers even called that way the "Death Road", but a Chinese climbing team was determined to make the climb.

In 1975, another Chinese team climbed to the top of Qomolangma to do research.
This time, they brought a ladder to the Second Step.
Until 2007, almost all climbers from the northern side used this "Chinese Ladder" to reach the top much faster.
In 2020, a Chinese research team went to Qomolangma to measure its height—8,848.86 metres.

Climbing Qomolangma is dangerous.
Some climbers reach the top successfully, but many fail.
Why do people still risk their lives to climb the highest mountain in the world?
It is because human curiosity and ambition cannot be stopped.
Or, as the English explorer George Mallory put it, it is simply "because it's there"!

Do you love the ocean?
Do you want to visit one of the natural wonders of the world?
If so, visit the Great Barrier Reef!

Located on the northeastern coast of Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is one of the most amazing places to visit.
It is the biggest coral reef in the world.
It takes up an area of 345,000 square kilometres and includes many islands and white sand beaches.
textTranslate:
对大多数人来说，珠穆朗玛峰是世界最大的奇迹之一。
站在地球之巅，你会觉得自己仿佛能够触碰到天空。
但只有最优秀的登山者才能登顶，而且他们必须先熬过恶劣的环境。
山上的气温可能会降至零下30摄氏度。
登山者还必须应对空气稀薄、悬崖峭壁和天气多变等困难。

1960年以前，还没有人能够从北坡登上珠穆朗玛峰顶。
登山者甚至把那条路称为“死亡公路”，但一支中国登山队决心登顶。

1975年，另一支中国登山队登上珠穆朗玛峰顶开展考察。
这一次，他们带了一架梯子到达第二台阶。
直到2007年，几乎所有从北坡攀登的登山者都使用这架“中国梯”，大大缩短了登顶时间。
2020年，一支中国考察队前往珠穆朗玛峰测量其高度——8,848.86米。

攀登珠穆朗玛峰十分危险。
有些登山者成功登顶，但许多人未能如愿。
为什么人们仍愿意冒生命危险攀登世界最高峰？
因为人的好奇心和雄心是无法阻挡的。
或者，正如英国探险家乔治·马洛里所说，只是因为“它就在那里”！

你喜欢大海吗？
你想游览世界自然奇观之一吗？
如果愿意，就去游览大堡礁吧！

大堡礁位于澳大利亚东北海岸，是最值得游览的绝美胜地之一。
它是世界上最大的珊瑚礁。
它占地345,000平方千米，包括许多岛屿和白沙滩。

title: Mount Lushan: A Mysterious Fairyland
titleTranslate: 庐山：神秘的仙境
text:
Mount Lushan is located in the south of Jiujiang, Jiangxi Province, near Poyang Lake. 171 peaks are found there.
Hanyang Peak, the highest peak of this mountain, is 1,474 metres high.
The Mount Lushan Scenic Area occupies 302 square kilometres, and it has been well known since ancient times for its great beauty.

The main attractions of the mountain include Wulao Peak, Xianren Cave, Lulin Lake, Hanpo Valley, Bailudong Academy, and many more.
The flow of the water and many other processes have made the many landscapes of the mountain.
There is a rich collection of landforms, such as rivers, lakes, and peaks.

Mount Lushan is also famous for its mist.
The mountain is covered in mist for nearly 200 days in a year.
Its average temperature is five or six degrees lower than that in the city.
It has been a famous summer resort since ancient times.

With its magnificent scenery and numerous historical sites, Mount Lushan is regarded as one of China's most famous mountains, and it was even included in the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1996.
textTranslate:
庐山位于江西省九江市南部，靠近鄱阳湖，共有171座山峰。
汉阳峰是庐山最高峰，海拔1,474米。
庐山风景区占地302平方千米，以秀美的景色闻名自古。

庐山的主要景点包括五老峰、仙人洞、鹿林湖、含鄱谷、白鹿洞书院等。
水流作用和其他许多过程共同塑造了庐山众多奇异的景观。
这里拥有丰富的地貌，如河流、湖泊和山峰。

庐山还以云雾闻名。
庐山一年中近200天云雾弥漫。
这里的平均气温比市区低五六摄氏度。
自古以来，庐山就是著名的避暑胜地。

庐山景色壮丽，历史遗迹众多，被誉为中国最著名的名山之一，并于1996年被列入《世界遗产名录》。

title: What happens during a natural disaster?
titleTranslate: 自然灾害发生时会发生什么？
text:
Haitao: H i, Lisa.
Did your family have any trouble during the typhoon?
Lisa: Yes, it was awful.
Haitao: I 'm sorry to hear that.
Did you know that a typhoon was coming?
Lisa: We did.
But it was worse than we expected.
We were driving home from our relatives' house when the strong winds started.
Haitao: Oh no!
It's dangerous to travel during a typhoon.
Lisa: I know.
It was raining hard while we were driving back.
We almost got into an accident when a truck nearly hit us.
Haitao: Oh dear, I'm glad you were safe!
Lisa: Yes, but when we got home later, we found water everywhere.
The house looked awful!
Was yours OK?
Haitao: Yes.
Luckily, we covered our windows and moved our things off the floor before the typhoon started.
We stored food and water too.
Lisa: That's good!
We'll do that next time.
textTranslate:
海涛：嗨，丽莎。
台风来袭时，你家人遇到什么麻烦了吗？
丽莎：是的，糟透了。
海涛：听到这件事我很难过。
你知道台风要来了吗？
丽莎：我们知道。
但情况比我们预想的还要糟糕。
我们从亲戚家开车回家时，狂风暴雨突然袭来了。
海涛：哦，不！
台风期间出行很危险。

一辆卡车险些撞上我们，我们差点酿成车祸。
海涛：哦，亲爱的，听说你们平安无事，我就放心了！

你家没事吧？

下次我们也这么做。

title: What can we do to prepare for the worst?
titleTranslate: 我们能为应对最坏的情况做哪些准备？
text:
On 26 December 2004, Tilly Smith, a 10-year-old English schoolgirl, and her family were on holiday in Phuket, Thailand.
Everyone was enjoying the beautiful weather that morning.
Some people were swimming in the sea, and some were relaxing on the beach.
But while Tilly was walking along the beach with her family, she noticed something strange.
Thick white froth was forming on top of the waves.
Next, she saw that the waves were coming in instead of going out.

Just then, she remembered something important.
Two weeks before, her geography teacher had explained that earthquakes under the sea could create dangerous waves called tsunamis!

"I know what's going to happen!
There's going to be a big wave," Tilly cried.
Unfortunately, her family didn't believe her and wanted to continue their walk.
However, Tilly refused to take a single step further.
Finally, her mother decided to continue the walk alone, and the rest of her family returned to the hotel.

Back at the hotel, Tilly's father told a security guard about the tsunami.
The security guard was shocked.
He knew about the huge earthquake in nearby Indonesia.
It meant that a tsunami was possible!
He jumped into action right away and rushed to get people off the beach.
Everyone began to panic.
People were screaming and running as fast as they could when they saw a huge wall of water coming from the sea.

Tilly was right!
Her mother was one of the last people on the beach, but thankfully, her family made it to safety just as the water hit the hotel.
The 2004 tsunami caused over 200,000 deaths, but no one on the beach died that day.

This true story shows how a single lesson could mean the difference between life and death.
Thanks to her knowledge and quick thinking, one schoolgirl was able to save over 100 lives.

Identifying the beginning, middle, and end of a story can help you understand the story better.
Look out for words and phrases that tell you when something happens, such as next, then, finally, when, while, and two weeks before.

Last Friday started terribly.
First, my alarm clock didn't go off, so I woke up late and had to rush to the bus stop.

I had a test that morning, so I was reviewing my notes while I was waiting for my bus.
All of a sudden, thunder rolled across the sky.
Then it started to pour.
The wind was too strong for me to use my umbrella!

By the time the bus came, I was cold and wet.
I was still worrying about the test when the bus driver said that we would be late.
There was a landslide along our usual road.

When I finally reached my classroom, out of breath, my teacher was already waiting at the door.
Many others were also late because of the rainstorm.
As a result, she said we weren't having a test after all!
What luck on my unlucky day!

During the hot and dry summer last year, my family experienced the first natural disaster of our lives.
We were hiking in the mountains when lightning flashed across the sky.
The sky got darker and darker.
And then we realized that we weren't looking at clouds.
It was smoke!
There was a wildfire!

Last winter, my family had a terrifying experience.
It started one evening while we were enjoying a quiet night at home.
My parents were watching TV while my brother was doing his homework.
I, on the other hand, was glued to my bedroom window.
Thick snow was falling and the world outside was growing whiter and whiter.
textTranslate:
2004年12月26日，10岁的英国女学生蒂莉·史密斯和家人正在泰国普吉岛度假。
那天早晨，所有人都在享受宜人的天气。
有人在海里游泳，有人在海滩上放松。
然而，蒂莉和家人在海滩上散步时，发现了一些奇怪的现象。
浪尖上形成了厚厚的白色泡沫。
接着，她发现海浪不是向外退去，而是向岸边涌来。

就在这时，她想起了一件重要的事。
两周前，她的地理老师曾讲解过，海底地震会引发被称为“海啸”的危险巨浪！

“我知道将要发生什么了！
就要来一个大浪了！”蒂莉喊道。
遗憾的是，她的家人不相信她，还想继续散步。
然而，蒂莉拒绝再向前走一步。
最后，她的母亲决定独自继续前行，的其他家人则返回了旅馆。

回到旅馆后，蒂莉的父亲把海啸的事告诉了保安。
保安听后十分震惊。
他知道附近的印度尼西亚发生了强烈地震。
这意味着有可能发生海啸！
他立即行动起来， rushed 去让人们离开海滩。
所有人都开始惊慌失措。
人们看到一堵巨大的水墙从海上逼近时，边尖叫边拼命奔跑。

蒂莉说得没错！
她的母亲是最后几个还在海滩上的人之一，幸运的是，就在海水冲向旅馆时，她的家人成功到达了安全地带。
2004年海啸造成超过20万人死亡，但那天海滩上没有人丧生。

这个真实的故事表明，一堂课就可能决定生死。
多亏她丰富的知识和敏捷的思维，一名女学生得以挽救100多条生命。

找出故事的开头、中间和结尾，有助于你更好地理解故事。
注意那些表明事情发生时间的词语和短语，如 next、then、finally、when、while 和 two weeks before。

上周五糟透了。
首先，我的闹钟没有响，所以我起晚了，不得不及忙赶往公交车站。

那天上午我要参加考试，等公交车时一直在复习笔记。

We watched a video first.
Through the video, we knew about what the doctors did.
They helped the wounded people immediately after the earthquake without thinking of their own safety.

After the video, one of the doctors showed us how to use a bandage and how to stop bleeding.
The lecture was helpful because we learnt how to help people when they are injured.

After that, another doctor shared his experience working in Wenchuan.
We were deeply moved by what he did.
And we clapped to show our respect to him.

Fifteen years have passed since the Wenchuan earthquake, yet the memories remain vivid.
Life is fragile when we are faced with the forces of nature.
But in China, no one stands alone, and assistance comes from all directions.
May the dead rest in peace, and may the living cherish their lives and continue to lend a helping hand to one another.

title: What Makes a True Gentleman
titleTranslate: 什么样的人才是真正的君子？
text:
A cultured man will respect others and will not go beyond what is right.
If he is respectful and observes the rules of propriety, then all men within the four seas will be fraternal to him.
Why need he worry about having no brothers? — The Analects of Confucius (Translated by Xu Yuanchong) A true gentleman is not someone who pretends to be noble or lonely.
Rather, he excels in communication.
A gentleman should be polite, respectful, and cautious with manners.
Good manners can help a gentleman to be loved by other people.
If everyone could behave with good manners, people all over the world could become brothers and sisters.
Then the world would live in peace and harmony.

During the Spring and Autumn Period, people in different states had different traditions and cultures.
But they were all a part of the same Chinese civilization and they shared many behaviours and ideas about good manners.

Confucius, a gentleman born in the Spring and Autumn Period, began to visit other states at the age of 55.
He always regarded the people he met along the way as his brothers.
He talked to the local people in a polite way and cared about their lives.
The locals were willing to talk about pressing and important matters with him.
Even people with different political views respected Confucius due to his good manners and noble ideals.
Confucius was taken to be a model nobleman.

title: The Origin of Red Envelopes During the Chinese Spring Festival
titleTranslate: 中国春节红包的由来
text:
In ancient times, there was a demon known as Sui.
On Chinese New Year's Eve, Sui would appear and touch the heads of sleeping children.
Unfortunately, this touch would make children cry.
To protect their little ones, parents would stay awake throughout the night and hope to drive Sui away.
This custom is called shousui.

Once, there was a couple who loved their son very much.
On the Eve, they were worried that Sui might harm their child.
To prevent this from happening, they decided to give their son some toys to keep him awake and out of Sui's reach.

The child's parents let him play with a few coins.
He placed them inside a red paper envelope.
Then he opened and closed the red envelope again and again while playing.
Finally, he fell asleep with the envelope of coins near his pillow.

At midnight, when Sui came, the coins began to glitter.
Frightened by the shining coins, Sui ran away in a hurry.
The couple was surprised to discover that the coins inside the red envelope had frightened Sui away!

After this, people started a custom of placing coins inside red envelopes and giving them to children as "lucky money" on the Eve of Chinese New Year.
This practice, known as yasuiqian, prevented Sui from returning.
To this day, we still keep this tradition.

So, if you think that playing the guitar is a waste of time, remember that this hobby is actually a great way to stay healthy!

In one study, after just 45 minutes of making art, most of the participants reported feeling more confident in themselves!

However, while hobbies have many benefits, it is important to find the right balance.
Playing computer games or chatting online may be fun, but such hobbies usually involve a lot of screen time.
That could cause problems such as eye strain or poor sleep.
These activities are also usually done alone, and that could cause some people to feel lonely.

Fresh air, green spaces, peace and quiet—these things help us to relax and feel good.
And if you go hiking or fly a kite in the park, you can take a friend with you!
Hanging out with friends reduces loneliness and can be a good way to build relationships.

Regardless of what your hobby is, it is important to make time for it.

演奏乐器还能让大脑保持年轻。
因此，如果你认为弹吉他是在浪费时间，请记住，这项爱好其实是一种保持健康的绝妙方式！

爱好对你的情绪健康也有好处。
绘画、写作等创造性爱好能帮助你排解负面情绪，为你提供表达感受的方式。
它们甚至能让你对自己感到满意！
在一项研究中，仅仅进行了45分钟艺术创作的多数参与者都表示，自己变得更加自信了！

然而，爱好虽然有许多益处，找到恰当的平衡仍然很重要。
玩电脑游戏或网上聊天可能很有趣，但这类爱好通常会占用大量屏幕时间。
这可能造成眼睛疲劳或睡眠不佳等问题。
这些活动通常也是独自进行的，这可能使一些人感到孤独。
为什么不选择一项户外爱好呢？
新鲜空气、绿色空间、宁静与安宁，这些都有助于我们放松身心、感受愉悦。
而且，如果你在公园里徒步或放风筝，还可以带上朋友！
与朋友一起消遣能减少孤独感，也有助于建立人际关系。

无论你的爱好是什么，为它留出时间都很重要。
毕竟，只工作不玩耍，杰克也会变笨！

title: All About Sneezing
titleTranslate: 喷嚏小知识
text:
If you had to list different ways of protecting yourself, sneezing probably would not be on the list.
But when you sneeze, that is exactly what is happening.
Sneezing helps you protect yourself from things like germs, dust, and smoke.
In fact, it is the body's way of getting rid of things that may harm you.

People cannot really control their sneezes.
If something starts tickling the inside of our nose, our brain takes over.
It knows that something inside the nose should not be there, so it sends a message to the body to get it out.

When we sneeze, many things happen in a very short time.
Usually, our eyes shut, our tongue presses against the top of our mouth, and the muscles in our stomach and chest get tight.
Next, a sudden blast of air comes out of our lungs and then our nose.
As the air goes out of our nose, it carries germs, dust, and tiny drops of water with it.

Some unusual things can also make us sneeze.
For example, some people sneeze when they look at a bright light.
If people have an allergy, certain plants or animals might also make them sneeze.
If they are allergic to certain plants, they might sneeze a lot in the seasons when the plants bloom, but not in others.
If they are allergic to dogs or cats, they usually cannot have one as a pet.

While sneezing is good for the person doing it, it can be very bad for the people nearby.
Sneezing is one way that diseases spread.
Millions of germs from one sneeze can travel up to about 8 metres at a speed of 160 kilometres per hour!
These germs can stay in the air, and if other people breathe in those germs, they can get sick too.
If you sneeze, always cover your nose and mouth.
After that, make sure to wash your hands.
Sneezing helps your body protect itself, but doing these two things can help you protect everyone else!
textTranslate:
如果要列出保护自己的各种方法，打喷嚏可能不会在名单上。
但当你打喷嚏时，事实恰恰如此。
打喷嚏能帮助你防御病菌、灰尘和烟雾等有害物质。
事实上，这是人体清除可能伤害自己的物质的一种方式。

人们无法真正控制自己的喷嚏。
如果鼻子里开始有东西使鼻腔发痒，我们的大脑就会接管这一过程。
大脑知道鼻子里不应该有异物，于是向身体发出信息，让它把异物排出来。

我们打喷嚏时，许多事情会在极短的时间内发生。
通常，我们的眼睛会闭上，舌头抵住上颚，腹部和胸部的肌肉也会绷紧。
接着，一股气流会突然从肺部喷出，然后从鼻孔排出。
气流从鼻孔排出时，会带出病菌、灰尘和细小的水滴。

一些不寻常的事情也会使我们打喷嚏。
例如，有些人在看到强光时会打喷嚏。
如果people对某些植物或动物过敏，他们也可能因此打喷嚏。
如果他们对某些植物过敏，在这些植物开花的季节可能会经常打喷嚏，而在其他季节则不会。
如果他们对狗或猫过敏，通常就不能饲养这类宠物。

打喷嚏对打喷嚏的人有益，但对身边的人可能非常有害。
打喷嚏是疾病传播的一种方式。
一次喷嚏产生的数百万个病菌可以飞散约8米，速度可达每小时160千米！
这些病菌可以悬浮在空气中，如果其他人吸入这些病菌，也可能会生病。
打喷嚏时，一定要捂住鼻子和嘴。
之后，务必洗手。
打喷嚏能帮助身体保护自己，但做这两件事也能帮助你保护其他人！

title: Laughter Is the Best Medicine
titleTranslate: 笑是最好的良药
text:
Do you often laugh with friends?
Do you giggle at jokes?
If you do, that is great, because just as the saying goes: Laughter is the best medicine!

People start laughing from a young age.
At around three months old, babies learn to laugh.
Even babies that cannot see or hear can laugh.
Laughter is a natural part of life!
But why is it so important?

First of all, laughter is good for our body.
When we laugh, our body takes in more oxygen.
Every part of our body needs oxygen to work well.
Laughter also makes our body work out.
Our heart, stomach, and even our shoulders work hard when we laugh!
But after we laugh, our muscles feel more relaxed.
A good laugh can help you feel relaxed for up to 45 minutes.
Over time, laughter helps our body to get stronger, fight off more diseases, and even create special chemicals to help us feel less pain!

Laughter also has many benefits for our mood.
When we laugh, it makes us feel less stressed or anxious, and things will not seem so bad.
Laughing also causes our brain to release chemicals that make us feel calm and happy.
Scientists even think that smiling often is enough to increase these chemicals in our brain.

But it is not always easy to laugh on our own.
We are 30 times more likely to laugh when we are around others.
According to some scientists, laughter can show others that we want to be close to them.
Monkeys clean one another's fur to show friendship.
But people laugh so that others will know that they are being friendly.

Some people even join laughing groups.
Although they force themselves to laugh at first, after hearing other people laugh, their laughter becomes real!
Before long, the whole group of people is laughing hard.

The next time you feel unhappy, try thinking about something funny.
Although you might not want to laugh when you are sad, doing so can make you feel better!
textTranslate:
你经常和朋友一起笑吗？
听到笑话你会咯咯笑吗？
如果会，那太好了，因为正如俗语所说：笑是最好的良药！

人们从很小的时候就开始笑了。
婴儿大约三个月大时，就学会笑了。
即使看不见或听不见的婴儿也会笑。
笑是生活中天然的一部分！
但笑为什么如此重要呢？

首先，笑对我们的身体有益。
我们笑的时候，身体会吸入更多氧气。
身体的每个部位都需要氧气才能正常运作。
笑还能让我们的身体得到锻炼。
我们笑的时候，心脏、胃，甚至肩膀都在辛勤工作！
但笑过之后，我们的肌肉会感觉更加放松。
痛快地笑一次，最多能让你放松45分钟。
久而久之，笑能帮助我们的身体增强免疫力、抵抗更多疾病，甚至产生特殊化学物质，帮助我们减轻疼痛！

笑对我们的情绪也有许多益处。
我们笑的时候，会感到压力和焦虑减轻，事情也不会显得那么糟。
笑还会促使大脑释放让我们感到平静和快乐的化学物质。
科学家甚至认为，经常微笑就足以增加大脑中这些化学物质的含量。

但我们独自一人时并不总是容易笑出来。
与别人在一起时，我们笑的可能性要高30倍。
一些科学家认为，笑能向别人表明我们希望与他们亲近。
猴子互相梳理毛发，以表示友谊。
但人类通过笑，让别人知道自己是在表示友善。

有些人甚至会加入笑闹小组。
虽然起初他们强迫自己发笑，但听到别人笑后，他们的笑就变成真心的了！
不一会儿，整组人就会放声大笑。

下次感到不开心时，试着想想有趣的事。
虽然伤心时你可能不想笑，但笑一笑会让你感觉好受些！

title: Unit 4 · The Sahara Desert
titleTranslate: 第4单元 · 撒哈拉沙漠
text:
Located in Africa, the Sahara Desert spreads across 30 per cent of the continent.
This vast desert, also known as "the great desert" in Arabic, is about 9 million square kilometres in size.
It is also at least 4.6 million years old.
This means that it is one of the oldest places in the world.

All deserts are dry, and the Sahara is both dry and hot.
It is the largest hot desert in the world.
We may think that all deserts are hot, but in fact some deserts are very cold!
Many scientists believe that Antarctica, for example, is a type of cold desert.

Most of the Sahara is rocky ground.
But there are also places with grass, lakes, mountains, and even sand seas.
A sand sea is just what it sounds like—it looks like a sea of sand!
When the wind blows, the sand looks like waves.

Life in the Sahara is difficult.
About two million people live in the Sahara.
They usually move from place to place.
There is water in a few parts of the Sahara, and some people live in these places all year round.

Not many animals can live in a place with such a dry and hot climate.
They must adapt to survive.
Camels, for example, go for a long time without drinking water.
When they do find water, they can drink more than 100 litres of it in 13 minutes!
Fennec foxes live in the desert too.
They have large ears to help their bodies stay cool.

Today, the world's largest hot desert is getting even bigger.
It is now about 10 per cent larger than what it was about a century ago.
But why is it growing?
Some scientists believe that part of the reason is climate change.
As temperatures rise, summers in Africa grow hotter and less rain falls.
Water bodies get smaller and the ground gets drier and drier.
If we do not take effective measures, the desert will keep growing!
textTranslate:
撒哈拉沙漠位于非洲，横跨非洲大陆的30%。
这片辽阔的沙漠在阿拉伯语中也被称为“大沙漠”，面积约为900万平方千米。
它的形成至少已有460万年。
这意味着它是世界上最古老的地方之一。

所有沙漠都很干旱，而撒哈拉沙漠既干旱又炎热。
它是世界上最大的热带沙漠。
我们可能认为所有沙漠都很炎热，但实际上有些沙漠非常寒冷！
例如，许多科学家认为南极洲属于一种寒冷沙漠。

撒哈拉沙漠大部分地区都是岩石地面。
但那里也有草地、湖泊、山脉，甚至沙海。
沙海正如其名——看起来就像一片沙子的海洋！
起风时，沙子看起来就像波浪。

撒哈拉沙漠里的生活十分艰难。
约有200万人生活在撒哈拉沙漠。
他们通常从一个地方迁徙到另一个地方。
撒哈拉沙漠的少数地区有水，有些人就终年居住在那里。

在气候如此干旱炎热的地方，能够生存的动物并不多。
它们必须适应环境才能生存。
例如，骆驼可以很长时间不喝水。
一旦找到水，它们能在13分钟内喝下100多升水！
耳廓狐也生活在沙漠中。
它们的大耳朵有助于身体保持凉爽。

如今，世界上最大的热带沙漠还在不断扩张。
它现在比大约一个世纪前大了10%左右。
但它为什么会扩大呢？
一些科学家认为，部分原因是气候变化。
随着气温上升，非洲的夏季变得更加炎热，降雨也减少了。
水域面积缩小，地面变得越来越干燥。
如果我们不采取有效措施，这片沙漠将继续扩大！

title: Unit 5 · Storm Chasing: A Dangerous but Important Job
titleTranslate: 第5单元 · 追风逐雨：一份危险却重要的工作
text:
Are you afraid of big storms?
Many people are.
But did you know some people go out to chase tornadoes?
Such storms can hit suddenly and move very quickly, so storm chasers always have to be prepared.

When a tornado is about to hit, professional storm chasers try and get close to it to collect important information.
Storm chaser Tim Samaras designed and built many different instruments for studying tornadoes.
Throughout his career, the engineer chased down more than 120 tornadoes.
Often, he filmed the storms while they were happening just a few kilometres away.

During a storm, storm chasers put special equipment in the way of the tornado.
The equipment collects information about things such as wind speed and air pressure.
This helps scientists to make better forecasts.
It can even help people understand how powerful the winds can be, and as a result, change how we build our houses.

Storm chasing can be exciting, but also very dangerous.
The storm chasers' knowledge and experience are not always enough to keep them safe.
On 31 May 2013, Samaras and his team were chasing the El Reno tornado in Oklahoma, USA.
To their surprise, the tornado behaved in an unexpected way.
It grew rapidly and changed its speed and direction.

On that terrible day, the largest tornado ever recorded appeared.
It was 4.2 kilometres wide and had winds topping 480 kilometres per hour.
While the tornado was moving towards them, Samaras and his team were driving as fast as they could.
Sadly, when the tornado hit their car, it threw their car into the air like a toy.
All three men in the car died.

The story of Tim Samaras is very sad, but his work continues to play an important role in weather science.
Though storm chasing remains a dangerous job, the goal of storm chasers is to learn more about storms to keep people safe.
For people like Samaras, that goal makes it all worth it.
textTranslate:
你害怕大风暴吗？
很多人害怕。
但你知道吗？有些人会外出追踪龙卷风。
这样的风暴可能突然袭击并迅速移动，因此龙卷风追踪者必须随时做好准备。

龙卷风即将袭来时，专业龙卷风追踪者会尽量靠近它，以收集重要信息。
龙卷风追踪者蒂姆·萨马拉斯设计和制造了许多用于研究龙卷风的不同仪器。
在其职业生涯中，这位工程师追踪过120多场龙卷风。
他经常在距离风暴只有几千米的地方拍摄风暴发生的过程。

风暴期间，龙卷风追踪者会把特殊设备放在龙卷风经过的路径上。
该设备会收集风速、气压等信息。
这有助于科学家作出更准确的预报。
它甚至能帮助人们了解风力有多强大，并据此改变房屋的建造方式。

追龙卷风可能令人兴奋，但也非常危险。
追龙卷风者的知识和经验并不总能保证他们的安全。
2013年5月31日，萨马拉斯和他的团队正在美国俄克拉何马州追捕埃尔雷诺龙卷风。
令他们惊讶的是，这场龙卷风的表现出乎意料。
它迅速扩大，并改变了速度和方向。

就在那个可怕的时刻，有记录以来最大的龙卷风出现了。
它宽达4.2千米， 风速最高超过每小时480千米。
当龙卷风朝他们逼近时，萨马拉斯和他的团队正拼命驾车疾驰。
遗憾的是，龙卷风击中他们的汽车后，像玩具一样将汽车掀到了空中。
车里的三名男子全部遇难。

蒂姆·萨马拉斯的故事非常悲惨，但他的工作仍在气象科学中发挥着重要作用。
尽管追龙卷风仍是一项危险的工作，但追龙卷风者的目标是进一步了解风暴，以保护人们的安全。
对萨马拉斯这样的人来说，这一目标使一切都值得。

title: Unit 6 · Symbols of Chinese Culture
titleTranslate: 第6单元 · 中国文化的象征
text:
Chinese culture is one of the oldest in the world, and it is rich in traditions and beliefs.
Many of the things you see, hear, or even taste in China may be symbols with special meanings!

In many Western stories, dragons are frightening monsters.
However, people in China are not frightened of them!
Instead, they think dragons are a symbol of power and good fortune.
Chinese dragons are so popular in China that you can see them in many places, such as vases, buildings, money, clothes, paintings, and jewellery!
The word for "dragon" even appears in names and idioms.
For example, "to hope that one's children become dragons" means that parents hope their children will do well in life.
In China, people think dragons are so powerful that they call themselves the descendants of the dragon!

In China, red is a powerful colour with special meaning.
Many people think it brings good luck and wealth, so you will see red decorations such as paper-cuts, couplets, and lanterns during festivals like the Chinese New Year.
People think red is so lucky that they wear it during celebrations.
At traditional Chinese weddings, both the bride and groom wear red.
Red also has positive meanings in other cultures.
For example, a red carpet shows importance, and red roses symbolize love.
However, in Western culture, red could sometimes mean loss.
If a company has "red ink" or is "in the red", it means that they are losing more money than they are earning.

Certain numbers are lucky in China because they sound like other Chinese words with positive meanings.
"Six", for example, sounds like "flow".
It symbolizes things going well.
The number "two" is also lucky, because the Chinese believe that good things come in pairs.
"Eight" sounds like a word which means "to make a fortune", and it symbolizes wealth.
Lastly, "nine" has the same pronunciation as the character "久", which means "long lasting".
So "nine" has come to symbolize a long life.
On the other hand, "four" sounds like "death".
Some people find this number so unlucky that they avoid using it in their phone numbers.
But China is not the only place with special numbers.
In America, for example, "seven" is a lucky number while "thirteen" is an unlucky number.
textTranslate:
中国文化是世界上最古老的文化之一，拥有丰富的传统和信仰。
你在中国看到、听到，甚至尝到的许多事物，都可能是具有特殊含义的象征！

在许多西方故事中，龙是可怕的怪物。
然而，中国人并不害怕龙！
相反，他们认为龙是力量和好运的象征。
中国龙在中国非常受欢迎，在花瓶、建筑、钱币、衣服、绘画和首饰上都能看到龙的形象！
“龙”这个词甚至还出现在姓名和习语中。
例如，“望子成龙”表示父母希望孩子在人生中取得成功。
在中国，人们认为龙非常强大，因此称自己为“龙的传人”。

在中国，红色是一种具有特殊含义的吉祥颜色。
许多人认为红色能带来好运和财富，因此在中国新年等节日期间，你会看到剪纸、对联和灯笼等红色装饰品。
人们认为红色非常吉利，因此庆典时会穿红色服装。
在中国传统婚礼上，新郎和新娘都穿红色服装。
红色在其他文化中也具有积极的含义。
例如，红地毯表示重要，红玫瑰象征爱情。
然而，在西方文化中，红色有时也表示损失。
如果一家公司出现“赤字”或处于“亏损”状态，就意味着它亏损的钱比赚的钱多。

在中国，一些数字之所以吉祥，是因为它们的读音与其他具有积极含义的汉字词语相似。
例如，“六”谐音“顺”。
它象征着事情进展顺利。
数字“二”也是吉祥的，因为中国人相信好事成双。
“八”谐音表示“发财”的词语，象征财富。
最后，“九”与汉字“久”读音相同，意思是“长久”。
因此，“九”逐渐成为长寿的象征。
另一方面，“四”谐音“死”。
有些人认为这个数字非常不吉利，甚至避免在电话号码中使用它。
但中国并不是唯一一个对数字有特殊看法的国家。
例如在美国，“七”是吉祥数字，而“十三”是不吉利的数字。

title: Unit 7 · The Story of Money
titleTranslate: 第7单元 · 钱的故事
text:
Long ago, there was no concept of money.
How did people acquire things they needed?
Let's explore the fascinating history of money.

In the beginning, people would exchange things they had on hand for other things to meet their own needs.
For instance, a shoemaker would trade his shoes with a baker for bread.
This way, the shoemaker acquired the bread he required, and the baker got the shoes he needed.
This practice was known as "bartering".

Bartering served its purpose for a while, but then a challenge appeared—the shoemaker needed bread every day, but the baker required only a few pairs of shoes each year.
How could they solve this problem?
The solution was the introduction of "money".

Early forms of money included salt, grain, shells, and even cattle.
However, these goods were hard to move or store.

Later, people agreed that some metal or paper was worth a certain amount of things like bread or shoes.
So they began to use metal or paper to make exchanges.
To simplify trade, people reached an agreement that certain metals or pieces of paper would represent specific values, equal to some bread or a number of shoes.
They could then use the metal or paper for business deals.
Around 1000 BCE, the use of metal money in the form of coins gained acceptance.

About three hundred years ago, paper money gained wider acceptance.
It was more convenient to carry and cost less to make than coins.
Eventually, paper money and coins became common in most countries worldwide.
Today, cashless payment is popular in some countries.
Money has become something that cannot be seen or touched.
textTranslate:
很久以前，还没有货币的概念。
人们是如何获得自己需要的东西的呢？
让我们一起探索货币那段迷人的历史。

最初，人们会用手头拥有的物品换取其他物品，以满足自己的需要。
例如，鞋匠会用自己做的鞋与面包师交换面包。
这样，鞋匠获得了自己需要的面包，面包师也得到了需要的鞋。
这种做法被称为“以物易物”。

以物易物在一段时间内发挥了作用，但后来出现了一个难题——鞋匠每天都需要面包，而面包师一年只需要几双鞋。
他们该如何解决这个问题呢？
解决方法是引入“货币”。

早期的货币形式包括盐、谷物、贝壳，甚至牲畜。
然而，这些物品不便于携带或储存。

后来，人们约定某些金属或纸张的价值相当于一定数量的面包或鞋子等物品。
于是，他们开始使用金属或纸张进行交换。
为了简化交易，人们达成协议，规定某些金属或纸片代表特定价值，相当于某些面包或一定数量的鞋子。
这样，他们就可以用金属或纸张进行交易。
约公元前1000年，以硬币形式出现的金属货币逐渐得到认可。

约三百年前，纸币得到更广泛的使用。
纸币比硬币更便于携带，制作成本也更低。
最终，纸币和硬币在世界上大多数国家变得普遍流通。
如今，无现金支付在一些国家十分流行。
货币已经变成了看不见、摸不着的东西。
